# Ezekiel 16 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 16:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-your-birth — on-the-day you-were-born your-navel-cord was-not-cut, and-in-water you-were-not-washed for-cleansing, and-you-were-not-salted, and-you-were-not-wrapped. |
| LOGOS | And as for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water to cleanse you, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling cloths. |
| PNEUMA | On the day you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord. No one washed you or rubbed you with salt or wrapped you in cloths. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 16:9 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-I-washed-you with-water, and-I-rinsed your-blood from-upon-you, and-I-anointed-you with-oil. |
| LOGOS | Then I bathed you with water and washed off your blood from you and anointed you with oil. |
| PNEUMA | I bathed you, washed the blood from you, and rubbed fragrant oil on your skin. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 16:10 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-I-clothed-you [with]-embroidered-work, and-I-shod-you [with]-fine-leather, and-I-wrapped-you in-fine-linen, and-I-covered-you [with]-silk. |
| LOGOS | I clothed you also with embroidered cloth and shod you with fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk. |
| PNEUMA | I dressed you in embroidered clothes and fine leather sandals. I wrapped you in linen and draped you in silk. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

## 16:12 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-I-put a-ring upon your-nose and-earrings upon your-ears and-a-crown-of beauty upon your-head. |
| LOGOS | And I put a ring on your nose and earrings in your ears and a beautiful crown on your head. |
| PNEUMA | a ring for your nose, earrings for your ears, and a magnificent crown for your head. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 16:13 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-you-were-adorned [with]-gold and-silver, and-your-clothing [was] fine-linen and-silk and-embroidered-work; fine-flour and-honey and-oil you-ate; and-you-were-beautiful, exceedingly, exceedingly, and-you-prospered to-royalty. |
| LOGOS | Thus you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was of fine linen and silk and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour and honey and oil. You grew exceedingly beautiful and advanced to royalty. |
| PNEUMA | You were adorned with gold and silver. Your clothes were fine linen, silk, and embroidery. You ate the finest flour, honey, and olive oil. You grew more and more beautiful, and you rose to be a queen. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 16:16 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-you-took from-your-garments and-made for-yourself high-places spotted, and-played-the-harlot upon-them — things-not-coming and-not shall-be. |
| LOGOS | You took your beautiful things and made pagan shrines, and played the harlot upon them — things that should not come to pass, nor ever shall be. |
| PNEUMA | You used your beautiful gifts to build pagan shrines and gave yourself to prostitution — outrageous acts that should never have happened. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.
